processing: A roasted-and-baked green tea from large-leaf bushes, combining pan-firing with oven drying; made in twisted strands and in tightly curled spirals.
harvest_season: Spring picking starts just after Qingming, at one bud with two or three leaves.
appearance_dry: Tight, sturdy, smooth strands with a grey-green bloom, or dense, glossy green spirals.
appearance_wet: Whole, tender buds and leaves of a bright yellow-green.
taste_profile: Rich and fresh with a strong roasted-chestnut aroma and a sweet return, more intense than most Chinese greens.

brewing.notes: Large-leaf green tea extracts strongly and can turn bitter, so go lighter on the leaf or shorter on the time rather than cooler on the water.

vintage_note: Sold as a current-year spring green tea, with picking beginning after Qingming, later than in lowland regions. Drink it within the year while the chestnut aroma is at its best. Check whether a pack means the protected county-wide Yunlong tea or the Dalishu factory product.
description:
Yunlong Green Tea comes from Yunlong county in Dali prefecture, western Yunnan, in the deep country between the Lancang and Nu rivers. It belongs to the broad Yunnan green family, known as Dian Lü, but is a pan-fired branch with a strong chestnut aroma and more concentration than the oven-dried norm.

The classic version comes from Dashantou at Dalishu in Baofeng township, at around 2,200 to 2,500 metres. It uses large-leaf bushes that bud late but give thick, soft shoots. Firing and baking are combined, and the tea appears as twisted strands or as tight spirals.

Expect a rich, sweet-finishing cup with that roasted-chestnut character and good staying power over several steeps. This is a sturdy green, and too much leaf or too long a steep brings out the bitterness of large-leaf tea.

The names overlap. Yunlong Green Tea is described as the Dalishu factory's product, while Yunlong Tea is the protected name covering eleven townships across the county. Ask which you are getting, and look for a date from this spring.
history:
The county gazetteer is cited as recording that in 1919 the magistrate Duan Tao bought 100 jin of tea seed from Shunning, now Fengqing, and handed it out for trials. Larger-scale planting began in 1987 in Baofeng, Jiuzhou and nearby areas.

Yunlong Green Tea took shape as a product made by the Dalishu tea factory under the supervision of the tea department of Yunnan Agricultural University. It carries a geographical-indication trademark, and China's agriculture ministry registered the wider Yunlong Tea name on 31 March 2016.
